extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants, agents, attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and substantive requirements for handling abandonment, petitions to withdraw a holding of abandonment, and petitions to revive abandoned patent applications under the MPEP and relevant 37 CFR provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatures required on forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatures of all the inventors or assignees of record of the entire interest or their representative(s) are required on the form(s). Submit multiple forms if more than one signature is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This collection of information is required by 37 CFR 1.138(c). Include typed or printed name and telephone number. Follow the form instructions for total number of forms submitted and mailing address (Mail Stop Express Abandonment, Commissioner for Patents).

rubrics_metrics.name: When an application is abandoned (37 CFR 1.135)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application becomes abandoned if applicant 'fails to reply' to an office action within the fixed statutory period, either by (A) failure to reply within the statutory period, or (B) insufficiency of reply (failure to file a 'complete and proper reply' within the statutory period).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an amendment is filed after expiration of the statutory period, the application is abandoned and the remedy is to petition to revive. Examiner should notify applicant by using Notice of Abandonment form PTOL-1432; late amendment is placed in the file wrapper but not formally entered (see MPEP § 714.17).

rubrics_metrics.name: Late amendment handling
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed after the expiration of the statutory period results in abandonment; the late amendment is placed in the file wrapper but not formally entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form PTOL-1432, check proper boxes and complete dates. Consider form paragraphs (e.g., 7.90, 7.98.02) for standard language. Do not mail a letter of abandonment until after the period for requesting an extension under 37 CFR 1.136(a) has expired. In pro se cases use form paragraph 7.98.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to revive — unavoidable delay (37 CFR 1.137(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to revive on the grounds that the failure to reply was unavoidable must be accompanied by: (1) the required reply (if filed), (2) a showing that the entire delay was unavoidable, (3) any required terminal disclaimer, and (4) the petition fee as set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(l).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The showing requirement can be met by submission of statements of fact establishing that the delay was unavoidable (including showing that any delay between abandonment and filing of the petition was unavoidable). No consideration to the substance of the petition will be given until the fee is received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to revive — unintentional delay (37 CFR 1.137(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to revive on the grounds that the failure to reply was unintentional must be accompanied by: (1) the required reply (if filed), (2) a statement that the entire delay was unintentional, (3) any required terminal disclaimer, and (4) the petition fee as set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may require additional information where there is a question whether the delay was unintentional. No consideration to the substance of the petition will be given until the fee is received. Submit required items promptly under a cover letter entitled 'Petition to Revive.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of the 'unavoidable' showing
rubrics_metrics.description: The showing for unavoidable delay must include statements of fact establishing that (1) the cause of the delay resulting in failure to reply was unavoidable, and (2) the cause of any delay between abandonment and filing the petition to revive was also unavoidable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide factual detail sufficient to satisfy the Director that the entire delay was unavoidable; include any supporting documentation as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer requirements on revival (37 CFR 1.137(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer (and fee per § 1.20(d)) is required with a petition to revive in: (1) design applications, (2) utility applications filed before June 8, 1995, and (3) plant applications filed before June 8, 1995. The terminal disclaimer must dedicate to the public a terminal part of the patent term equivalent to the period of abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The terminal disclaimer must also apply to any patent granted on any application containing a specific reference under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121 or 365(c) to the application for which revival is sought. Paragraph (d)(1) provisions do not apply to revival sought solely for copendency with applications filed on or after June 8, 1995, to lapsed patents, reissue applications, or reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: No substantive consideration until petition fee received
rubrics_metrics.description: No consideration to the substance of a petition to revive will be given until the applicable petition fee is received (per 37 CFR 1.17(l) or 1.17(m)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the correct fee is submitted with the petition; petitions without the fee will not be acted upon substantively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits and extensions for petitions and reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions under 37 CFR 1.181 not filed within two months of the mailing date of the action or notice complained of may be dismissed as untimely. A request for reconsideration of a refusal to revive must be filed within two months of the decision refusing to revive (unless otherwise set).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless a decision indicates otherwise, the two-month period may be extended under specific provisions: § 1.136 for abandoned applications/lapsed patents; § 1.550(c) for terminated ex parte reexamination; § 1.956 for terminated inter partes reexamination. Mere filing of a petition will not stay any running period for reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficiency of reply (reply not fully responsive)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant's reply that is within the period for reply but not fully responsive to the Office action may result in abandonment; the reply must be 'complete and proper' as the condition of the case may require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reply is a bona fide attempt and substantially a complete reply but inadvertently omitted something, applicant may be given a new time under § 1.134 to supply the omission. Use form paragraph 7.91 when appropriate; if the reply appears to be a bona fide attempt with inadvertent omission, use form paragraph 7.95 instead of 7.91. In form paragraph 7.91, explain why reply not fully responsive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common situations causing abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Various procedural events can cause abandonment, including: copying claims from a patent (when not suggested by the Office) does not constitute a reply; withdrawal/failure to prosecute an appeal; dismissal of an appeal or civil action without filing an amendment putting the application in condition for issue; improper RCE filing that withdraws an appeal; filing a CPA under 37 CFR 1.53(d); failure to timely pay issue or publication fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See cited MPEP sections for each scenario (e.g., § 1215.01–1215.04 for appeals, § 706.07(h) for RCE issues). An improper RCE will not toll time periods set in prior Office actions; payments (issue/publication fees) must be paid to cure abandonment for nonpayment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to withdraw holding of abandonment vs. petition to revive
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.181 to withdraw a holding of abandonment is appropriate where applicant contends there was no abandonment in fact (e.g., disagreement as to sufficiency of reply or controlling dates) and does not require a fee. Where there is no dispute as to whether an application is abandoned (only the cause is contested), a petition under 37 CFR 1.137 (revival) with the appropriate fee is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand the distinction: use 1.181 when contesting the holding of abandonment (fee-free); use 1.137 when revival is required because abandonment did occur. Two-month timeliness rules under 1.181(f) apply to petitions to withdraw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing of nonreceipt of an Office action (petition to withdraw)
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish nonreceipt of an Office communication, practitioner must describe the system used for recording an Office action received at the correspondence address of record and show the docketing system is sufficiently reliable; the record should include application number, attorney docket number, mail date and due date for response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit copies of master docket reports, file jackets, incoming mail logs, calendars, reminder systems, or individual docket records demonstrating the action was not entered. If no master docket exists, state that and provide other evidence. Nonreceipt evidence may be insufficient if practitioner has a history of not receiving Office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of timely mailing or filing (Express Mail, postcard receipts, certificates of mailing)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to withdraw based on timely mailing may rely on Express Mail procedures (37 CFR 1.10(c)-(g)), postcard receipts (prima facie evidence of timely filing), or a certificate of mailing under 37 CFR 1.8(b) with a statement under 1.8(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When shown mailed via Express Mail, enter paper in PALM with the Express Mail date. When relying on a postcard receipt, enter reply into PALM using the receipt date. For certificates of mailing, the attesting statement must be on a personal knowledge basis or otherwise satisfy the Director; if not personally made by signer, include supporting evidence (mailing logs). If notifying Office of prior mailing under 1.8(b) after a reasonable time, submit duplicate copy and statement; check private PAIR before notifying Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of untimely petitions to withdraw the holding of abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.181(f) permits dismissal of petitions not filed within two months of the action complained of. The Office may, instead of dismissal, require a terminal disclaimer as a condition of granting an untimely petition to withdraw.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For design applications, utility applications filed before June 8, 1995, and plant applications filed before June 8, 1995, a petition to withdraw not filed within two months of the notice of abandonment will not be treated on its merits (absent extraordinary circumstances) unless accompanied by a terminal disclaimer under 37 CFR 1.321(a) and the fee under 37 CFR 1.20(d). The period to be disclaimed runs from two months after the mail date of the notice of abandonment to the filing date of a grantable petition to withdraw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and effect of petitions and PALM entry rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reply is shown timely filed by Express Mail or postcard receipt, entry into PALM must reflect the mailing/receipt date per the applicable proof mechanism; when relying on certificates of mailing, enter correspondence with the actual date of receipt (date duplicate copy filed with 1.8 statement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow PALM entry rules: Express Mail date for Express Mail; postcard receipt date for postcard; certificate of mailing entries use actual date of receipt. Ensure supporting documentary proof accompanies petitions relying on those proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms and form paragraphs to use for abandonment and replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific form paragraphs and forms are prescribed for abandonment and related notices (e.g., PTOL-1432 Notice of Abandonment; form paragraphs 7.90, 7.98.02, 7.91, 7.95).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate form paragraph depending on the circumstances (e.g., 7.98.02 for pro se late reply advising petition to revive under 1.137; 7.91 for reply not fully responsive; 7.95 for bona fide attempts with inadvertent omission). Complete required blanks and examiner notes per MPEP instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival reply methods for different abandonment causes
rubrics_metrics.description: The required 'reply' for purposes of revival varies by abandonment type: in nonprovisional applications abandoned for failure to prosecute, the required reply may be met by filing a continuing application; in nonprovisional utility or plant applications filed on or after June 8, 1995, the required reply may be met by filing a Request for Continued Examination (RCE) in compliance with § 1.114; for abandonment due to failure to pay issue or publication fees, the reply must include payment of those fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the reply submitted with a petition to revive satisfies the specific requirements for the abandonment type (continuing application, compliant RCE, or fee payment as applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival of provisional applications and pendency limit
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application abandoned for failure to timely respond may be revived pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137, but subject to 35 U.S.C. 119(e)(3) and § 1.7(b), a provisional application will not be regarded as pending after twelve months from its filing date under any circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely awareness of provisional pendency limits is required; revival may not restore pendency beyond 12 months from filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to the Director (37 CFR 1.181) — scope and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to the Director under 37 CFR 1.181 may be taken from any action or requirement of any examiner in ex parte prosecution of an application, or in ex parte or inter partes prosecution of a reexamination proceeding not subject to appeal to the Board. Filing a petition does not stay any period for reply nor act as a stay of other proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any petition not filed within two months of the mailing date of the action or notice may be dismissed as untimely, except as otherwise provided. For petitions involving Board actions, see § 41.3. Understand that petition filing alone does not suspend running statutory periods.
